title: The rulebook's modes: build for tetrises, dig or survive in trouble
intro: Press play to walk the full build → trouble → recover cycle over the recorded seed-607 run. The board beside each step is the real recorded position.

walk.title: BUILD — the default mode
walk.text: On a clean, low stack it builds a 9-1 stack: nine columns packed flat plus one open well on the right edge, saving I-pieces to clear four lines at once. The 9-1 shape was self-evolved — nobody hand-coded it; it fell out of the training climb.

in.label: a real recorded build position
in.from: recorded from the Reflexer (rulebook search) lane, seed 607, 2026-09-25, arena/demo_oracle.json _meta.sources.tetris_rulebook · katgpt-rs examples/tetris_09_site_walk.rs · turn 271 (the strongest 9-1 build position)

walk.title: Trouble #1 — covered holes → DOWNSTACK
walk.text: Three or more holes buried under the stack and building stops paying: every new piece makes it worse. The mode flips to DOWNSTACK, which deliberately clears the lines sitting above the holes to dig them back out.

walk.title: Trouble #2 — tall stack → SURVIVE
walk.text: A stack twelve rows high is one bad piece from topping out. SURVIVE takes any line it can and keeps the board low — scoring gives way to staying alive. (Survive wins when both exits fire at once.)

walk.title: Recovery — both modes hand back to BUILD
walk.text: Holes dug out, or the stack back under twelve — either way the mode returns to BUILD and the cycle starts over. The board is re-read before every single piece, so the switch is never late.

in.label: a real recovered position
in.from: recorded from the Reflexer (rulebook search) lane, seed 607, 2026-09-25, arena/demo_oracle.json _meta.sources.tetris_rulebook · katgpt-rs examples/tetris_09_site_walk.rs · turn 80 (holes dug out, stack back under 12)

walk.title: One search, three weights
walk.text: The modes are not three different AIs — it is the same placement search wearing different score weights: self-evolved builder weights while safe, proven survival weights in trouble. That is the whole trick behind the rulebook lane.
